title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper proposes the proximity kernel, a similarity measure for incomplete data that uses equal-frequency binning and Voronoi-based proximity assignment to create a density-adaptive high-dimensional sparse representation without explicit imputation. Missing values are handled by a cascading fallback strategy that uses kernel mean embedding over progressively relaxed matching sets: intersection-based exact matching, union-based partial matching, and global prior distributions. Experiments on 12 UCI datasets show that the method achieves the highest average NMI (0.4245) in K-means clustering compared to 9 baselines while maintaining linear time complexity.

match_target.why: The user hint explicitly targets Table 3, proximity kernel NMI on Hepatitis with K-means. This is the cheapest claim to reproduce (155 samples, 19 features, < 1 min on CPU) while still exercising the full pipeline: equal-frequency binning, proximity assignment, one-hot encoding, cascading fallback for missing values, and K-means clustering on the resulting representation.

tolerance.why: NMI is a bounded score in [0,1] printed as a fraction (0.2289). The Hepatitis dataset has 155 samples, which is fewer than 2,000 examples. Rule 3 applies: 0.02 absolute for a bounded score on a smaller set printed in [0,1].

requirements.stmt: Bin centers must be selected via equal-frequency binning using only observed (non-missing) values for each feature.
requirements.quote: The bin centers cj,kare determined by computing evenly-spaced percentiles of the observed distribution

requirements.stmt: Each observed value must be assigned to its nearest bin center (proximity assignment), creating a Voronoi-like partition.
requirements.quote: we assign each observed value to its nearest center

requirements.stmt: Observed features must be encoded as one-hot binary vectors of length nbins per feature.
requirements.quote: we encode each feature using one-hot representation

requirements.stmt: Missing value handling must use a three-level cascading fallback: Level 1 intersection-based exact matching across all observed features.
requirements.quote: The intersection-based matching set S1(i) is the intersection across all observed features

requirements.stmt: If Level 1 fails, fallback to Level 2 union-based partial matching across any observed feature.
requirements.quote: We define the union-based matching set as: S2(i) = ∪ j∈Oi Ci,j

requirements.stmt: If Level 2 fails, fallback to Level 3 global prior distribution computed from observed feature marginals.
The proximity kernel must be defined as the normalized inner product of the encoding vectors: K(xm,xn) = (1/d) zm^T zn.
requirements.quote: We define the proximity kernel between samples mand nas: K(xm,xn) = 1 dzT mzn

requirements.stmt: Clustering must use K-means with the number of clusters set to the ground-truth number of classes for each dataset.
requirements.quote: we applied K-means with the number of clusters to the ground-truth number of classes

requirements.stmt: Clustering quality must be evaluated using Normalized Mutual Information (NMI).
requirements.quote: we evaluate all methods on clustering quality using Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) as the metric

requirements.stmt: Each experiment must be conducted 10 times and the average result reported for stability.
requirements.quote: Each experiment was conducted 10 times and report average results for stability

requirements.stmt: The number of bins per feature (nbins) must be searched over the set {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}.
requirements.quote: we search the number of bins per dimension in {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}

requirements.quote: All of these datatsets are from UCI datasets

data.name: UCI Machine Learning Repository (12 datasets: Kidney, Mammography, Heart, Hepatitis, Horse, Wisconsin Breast Cancer, Credit Approval, Adult, Voting, Mushroom, Primary Tumor, Soybean)
data.how_to_get: Download from https://archive.ics.uci.edu/datasets. Dataset names in the paper map to standard UCI dataset names (e.g., 'Mammo' = Mammographic Mass, 'M.room' = Mushroom, 'Wiscom' = Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer).
